scenes.title: Multi-Region & Disaster Recovery
scenes.narration: Disaster recovery plans how your data platform survives the loss of an entire region, balancing recovery speed against cost with well-chosen strategies.

scenes.title: The Two Key Objectives
bullets: The recovery time objective defines how quickly you must be running again after a disaster.
The recovery point objective defines how much recent data you can afford to lose.
Tighter objectives cost more, so you match the strategy to the business need.
scenes.narration: Disaster recovery planning centers on two targets. The recovery time objective sets how fast you must restore service. The recovery point objective sets how much recent data loss is tolerable. Both drive cost, so the art is matching a strategy to what the business actually requires rather than over-engineering.

scenes.title: DR Strategies by Cost
steps: Pilot light: core running, scale on failover
scenes.narration: Disaster recovery strategies form a spectrum. Backup and restore is cheapest but recovery is slow. A pilot light keeps core components running to speed things up. A warm standby maintains a scaled-down live copy, and active-active runs full capacity in multiple regions for near-instant failover. Cost rises as recovery time shrinks.

scenes.title: RTO vs. RPO
scenes.narration: The recovery time objective governs how much downtime you can accept and therefore how ready your standby must be. The recovery point objective governs how much data you can lose and therefore how frequently you must replicate or back up. Setting both explicitly is the first step of any credible DR plan.

scenes.title: Cross-Region Replication for Backups
scenes.narration: This S3 replication rule automatically copies critical data to a bucket in another region. Objects under the critical prefix are replicated to a disaster-recovery bucket in a second region using cost-efficient infrequent-access storage. Should the primary region fail, a recent copy of your most important data already waits safely elsewhere.

scenes.text: Set explicit RTO and RPO targets, then pick the cheapest DR strategy that meets them — from backups to active-active as the stakes rise.
scenes.narration: Define your recovery time and recovery point objectives first, then choose the least costly strategy that satisfies them. As business criticality grows, you move up the ladder from simple backups toward full active-active resilience.
